2027-05-04.title: Tuesday of the Sixth Week of Easter
readings: Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household
Your right hand delivers me, O Lord (or: Alleluia)
It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you
2027-05-04.alt: Easter weekday of the sixth week (Year I). The Alleluia is sung before the Gospel, the paschal candle burns beside the ambo, and the Regina Caeli takes the place of the Angelus until Pentecost. The Church is now turning towards the Ascension and the coming of the Holy Spirit. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-05-04.verse: Nevertheless I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
theo: Paul and Silas have barely arrived in Philippi, the first city of Macedonia where the Gospel is preached, when trouble begins. They have driven a spirit of fortune-telling out of a slave girl, and her owners, who made money from her, drag them before the magistrates. The crowd joins in; the magistrates have them stripped and beaten with rods, and they are thrown into the innermost cell with their feet fastened in the stocks. Then comes one of the most beautiful sentences in the Acts of the Apostles: “About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.” Bleeding, chained, in the dark, they sing. Suddenly an earthquake shakes the foundations, the doors fly open and everyone's chains are unfastened. The jailer wakes, sees the open doors, and draws his sword to kill himself, for a Roman jailer who lost his prisoners could pay with his life. “But Paul shouted in a loud voice, ‘Do not harm yourself, for we are all here.’” The prisoners have not fled. The jailer falls trembling before them and asks the question of every human heart: “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?” The answer is simple: “Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.” That same night the jailer washes their wounds, and he and his family are baptized. He brings them into his house, sets food before them, and “he and his entire household rejoiced that he had become a believer in God.” The night that began with beatings ends with Baptism and a meal of joy.

The Psalm is the song of Paul and Silas at midnight: “I give you thanks, O Lord, with my whole heart.” “On the day I called, you answered me, you increased my strength of soul.” And even in the middle of trouble: “you stretch out your hand, and your right hand delivers me.” In the Gospel Jesus prepares the disciples for his going away. They are full of sorrow; they cannot imagine life without him. But he tells them something surprising: “it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.” The Ascension is not a loss but the condition of a greater gift. While Jesus walked in Galilee he could be in only one place at a time; through the Holy Spirit he will be present in every disciple, in every prison cell and every home. And the Spirit will “prove the world wrong about sin and righteousness and judgment”: he will show that the real sin is refusing to believe in Jesus, that the one condemned on the cross was the righteous one now gone to the Father, and that the ruler of this world, not Jesus, has been judged. The same Spirit sang in Paul and Silas at midnight, shook the prison, and turned a jailer into a brother. In these days before the Ascension, the Church learns to trust that the Lord who goes away is not leaving us alone.
outline: Ask: what would you do at midnight in prison, after a beating?
Praise in the dark, and the prisoners listening.
Point 2 · What must I do to be saved?
The jailer's question and the Gospel's answer.
The Ascension makes room for the Advocate.
“If I go, I will send him to you.”
live: When something goes wrong today, pause and say or sing one line of praise before you say anything else.
Think of one person who is near despair. Pray for them by name today, and send them a word of hope.
2027-05-04.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you went away to the Father so that the Advocate might come to us. As Paul and Silas sang to you at midnight, teach us to praise you in our darkest hours. Stretch out your right hand and deliver all who are imprisoned, in body or in spirit. Send us your Holy Spirit, to convince the world of the truth and to make us messengers of salvation to everyone who asks, what must I do to be saved? Amen.
altar: After his Baptism the jailer of Philippi “set food before them” and the whole household rejoiced. The first Christians often joined Baptism and a meal of joy. At the altar the risen Lord himself sets food before the baptized: his own Body and Blood, the meal of those who have been saved.

quick: In Philippi Paul and Silas were beaten and jailed; at midnight they prayed and sang, and an earthquake opened the doors.
Paul stopped the jailer from killing himself; the jailer asked how to be saved and was baptized with his household.
Jesus says it is better for the disciples that he goes away, so that the Advocate may come.
2027-05-04.action: Turn one moment of frustration today into a moment of praise.
2027-05-04.question: Do I believe that the Lord's “going away” in my life can make room for a greater gift?

family.explain: Paul and Silas were put in prison for talking about Jesus. Their feet were locked. But at midnight, instead of crying, they sang songs to God! Then an earthquake opened all the doors. The jailer was so amazed that he asked to know Jesus, and his whole family was baptized that night.
family.intention: We pray for people who are in prison, and for their families waiting at home.
family.ask: Ask: “What song can we sing to God when we are sad?” Choose one hymn and sing it together tonight.

illus: Blessed Rani Maria, the Franciscan Clarist sister from Pulluvazhy near Perumbavoor, worked among the poor in Madhya Pradesh and was murdered in 1995. Her killer, Samundar Singh, was sent to prison. There, years later, her own sister, Sister Selmy Paul, visited him, called him brother, and tied a rakhi on his wrist. He wept, asked forgiveness, and was later received with love by the family of the one he had killed. Like the jailer of Philippi, a man in the darkness found his way to salvation because Christians answered violence with mercy.

pm.open: Lord, at midnight Paul and Silas sang your praises. Teach us to praise you in every hour, and send us your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God (Acts 16:25). What do I do in my midnight hours?
Sirs, what must I do to be saved? (Acts 16:30). Who around me is asking this question, perhaps without words?
It is to your advantage that I go away (John 16:7). What loss in my life has made room for a greater gift?
pm.resp: Your right hand delivers me, O Lord.
interc: For prisoners and prison chaplains, that the light of Christ may reach them.
For those who are thinking of harming themselves, that someone may say to them, as Paul did: do not harm yourself.
For families who are preparing for Baptism, that the joy of the jailer's household may be theirs.
For victims of violence and for those who have hurt them, that mercy may open the way to conversion.
For our group, that the Holy Spirit may fill us as we prepare for the Ascension and Pentecost.
pm.close: Father, you answered Paul and Silas at midnight. Stretch out your hand over all who suffer, and send us the Advocate, as your Son promised. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, picture the scene. Paul and Silas have been stripped and beaten with rods in Philippi. They are in the innermost cell, their feet locked in the stocks. It is dark, it is cold, every bone aches. And about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them (Acts 16:25).

The other prisoners were listening. People are always listening to how Christians suffer. When we complain, curse and despair, they hear. When we pray and praise God in the middle of pain, they hear that too. A Christian singing at midnight is one of the strongest sermons in the world.

Then the earthquake, the open doors, the jailer with his sword. And Paul's cry: do not harm yourself, for we are all here (Acts 16:28). The prisoners could have run away; they stayed, and their staying saved a life. The jailer asks: what must I do to be saved? Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household (Acts 16:31). By morning there is a baptized family and a joyful meal.

In the Gospel Jesus says something hard: it is to your advantage that I go away (John 16:7). The disciples could not understand. How could losing him be good? But if he does not go, the Advocate will not come. In a few days we will celebrate his Ascension, and then Pentecost. He goes so that his Spirit can be with each of us, everywhere, even in a prison at midnight. Let us trust him in our losses, praise him in our darkness, and wait for the Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, Paul and Silas were in jail, with their feet locked up. Did they cry? No, they sang songs to God in the middle of the night! Then God sent an earthquake and the doors opened. The jailer was so amazed that he and his family came to know Jesus. When you are sad or scared, try singing a little song to Jesus. He hears you!

intro: Theme: “If I go, I will send him to you.”
Praise at midnight, a jailer's question, and the gift that comes through the Lord's going away.

q: By day the Lord commands his steadfast love, and at night his song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
points.apply: Learn one short hymn or psalm verse by heart this week and use it whenever you feel low.

points.h: What must I do to be saved?
q: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
They answered, “Believe on the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.”
points.apply: Reach out this week to someone who seems close to despair, and stay with them as Paul stayed with the jailer.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you;
Nevertheless I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
points.apply: Begin today to pray each evening, until Pentecost: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.

concl: Paul and Silas sang in the dark, and the Spirit turned a prison into a place of Baptism.
The Lord who goes to the Father sends the Advocate, so that he may be with us everywhere, even at midnight.
2027-05-04.resolve: Praise God in one difficulty each day this week, and pray for the Holy Spirit every evening.
